title: dynamic-batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding minimization heuristics
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Context: We see significant padding overhead for dynamic batching when request sequence lengths are widely distributed. Motivation: reduce wasted compute and memory by grouping requests into buckets by sequence length and selecting padding targets that minimize overall token padding while preserving latency SLOs. Design: 1) Bucketing: compute runtime quantile buckets (default: P0-P50, P50-P80, P80-P95, P95-P100) per route over a sliding window and maintain an adaptive bucket map. 2) Padding target selection: pick per-bucket padding targets by minimizing (estimated padded_tokens * kernel_cost(sequence_length)) subject to tail-latency constraints using lightweight cost heuristics. 3) Scheduler integration: continuous-batching scheduler now prefers forming batches inside the same bucket and will opportunistically merge adjacent buckets when latency slack allows. 4) KV cache/placement: KV cache keys are annotated with bucket id; we now co-locate KV caches for similar seqlen buckets to increase reuse and reduce evictions. 5) Fallbacks: when bucketing increases wait time for low-traffic buckets, the scheduler falls back to size-based batching or immediate-execution if latency SLOs would be missed. 6) Telemetry: added per-bucket metrics (padded_tokens, batch_size_distribution, batch_wait_ms) and new alerts when padding ratio increases beyond threshold. Implementation details: runtime changes in runtime/batching.rs implement bucketing and padding heuristics; scheduler changes in runtime/scheduler.rs add bucket-aware queueing and soft-deadline merging logic; KV cache tags added in runtime/kv_cache.rs with migration helpers; Python SDK route-level overrides added in redwood-sdk-python to allow customers to opt-out or tune bucket windows. Benchmarks: synthetic microbench with mixed seqlen distribution (mix of 16/64/256/1024 tokens) shows throughput improvement of 7-12% on A100 for greedy decode and up to 18% improvement for beam setups due to reduced padding; cost-savings (tokens processed) ranged 10-30% depending on workload skew. Latency: median latency unchanged, p99 within 5% (configurable). Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to canary customers for two weeks; monitor padded_tokens, tail latency, error rates; staged rollout to 100% after metric stability. Docs/compat: added SDK docs and runtime tuning guide. Checklist: [x] design doc linked [x] unit tests [x] perf benchmarks [x] backward-compatible config [x] migration helpers [x] metrics and dashboards. Related: ENG-3482 (batching roadmap), ENG-3590 (kv-cache eviction improvement).

review_comments:
Jonas Reed: Nice work — can you quantify how often we end up merging adjacent buckets in production? Would love a telemetry counter.
Aisha: Added per-bucket merge_count metric and included in dashboards.

Marta Chen: Concern: annotating KV cache keys increases key cardinality; any eviction/GC implications?
Aisha: We co-locate caches and added an eviction policy that groups by bucket to avoid premature evictions; added tests and bench to validate.

Liam O'Connor: Does this interact with quantization/kernel selection? If padding causes sequence lengths to hit power-of-two boundaries we may get faster kernels.
Aisha: Yes — cost model includes kernel preference; heuristic favors padding targets that map to efficient kernel lengths when beneficial.

Marta Chen: Please ensure runbooks include how to disable per-route bucketing when debugging.
Aisha: Added SDK override and runbook entry in docs.

Jonas Reed: Approving pending a small lint fix in scheduler tests.
Aisha: Fixed and pushed.

release_notes: Added dynamic sequence-length bucketing and padding minimization heuristics for runtime batching. Default is opt-in via feature flag. Expected benefits: reduced padding overhead, improved throughput and lower token processing costs for skewed workloads. See docs/runtime/bucketing.md for tuning.
